summary: Iteration 103 verified all 3 bug fixes end-to-end. BUG A (archive scroll no-flicker): PASSED with runtime instrumentation — sampled the pill's wrapper opacity every 100ms for 3000ms after tapping [data-testid=archive-scroll-top]; max_opacity_after_200ms=0.000, opacity stayed at 0.00 for the ENTIRE 3s window, scrollTop reached 0 within 300ms. The 3s fallback timer + onMomentumScrollEnd/onScrollEndDrag gates work together to fully suppress mid-animation onScroll re-toggles. BUG B (per-notif red border persistence + individual tap clear): PASSED completely. Seeded 16 unread notifs for chat_a. Initial view rendered 16/16 with borderWidth:2px + borderColor:rgb(255,69,58). CRITICAL: after navigating to home tab and back to notifications, ALL 16/16 STILL rendered with red 2px border (this was the previously-broken behavior — now fixed). Server confirmed 16/16 unread on that visit. Tapping ONE unread notif flipped ONLY that row (bw:2px→1px, bc:red→gray) while the other 15 remained red. Server confirmed unread count decremented by exactly 1 (16→15) and the tapped notif_id had read=true persisted. BUG C (native logout crash on flaky network): PASSED via code inspection as requested — (i) router.replace('/auth') is called at line 221 BEFORE logout() runs, (ii) logout is invoked with {skipStateUpdates:true} at line 226 so setUser(null) never fires, (iii) navStack dynamic import is wrapped in an async IIFE (lines 230-235) so it can't block, (iv) all awaits inside doLogout are fire-and-forget with .catch(()=>{}). Backend regression: 11/11 pytest tests passed covering new endpoint POST /api/notifications/{notif_id}/read (mark-single, idempotent, wrong-owner noop, auth-required), bulk mark-read still works, and /api/auth/logout is idempotent across 4 scenarios (valid token, no token, bad token, called twice).
critical_code_review_comments: archive.tsx lines 272-291: onScroll gate + onMomentumScrollEnd + onScrollEndDrag correctly release suppressScrollUpdatesRef only when the actual scroll settles, and re-evaluate showTopBtn from the final scroll position. Combined with the 3s onPress fallback timer (line 332) this is defence-in-depth against the previous flicker.

notifications.tsx onPress lines 132-169: correctly performs optimistic setItems mutation BEFORE calling router.push, so React commits the read-state re-render synchronously with the click. Per-item api.notificationMarkOneRead is fire-and-forget with a .then(refreshBadge) so the bell-icon tab-badge decrements. useFocusEffect (lines 77-90) reloads items but DOES NOT call bulk mark-read — this is the fix for step 3 (nav away and back preserves red borders on remaining unread notifs).

profile.tsx doLogout native path (lines 210-236): router.replace called BEFORE logout(), logout invoked with {skipStateUpdates:true}, all awaits wrapped in try/catch, navStack import inside async IIFE. Crash-proof under flaky network as specified.

server.py POST /notifications/{notif_id}/read at line 3509: correctly scopes the update to {notif_id, user_id} so users can't mark others' notifs read. Returns {updated: modified_count}. Note: the filter does not include {read:False}, so calling on an already-read notif returns updated=1 (because read_at gets a new timestamp); this is behaviourally idempotent (no error) but modified_count could theoretically be used to short-circuit UI refreshes. Non-blocking observation.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (BUG A + BUG B verified with runtime instrumentation, BUG C verified via code inspection as requested)

seed_data_creation: db.notifications.updateMany({user_id:'user_6e65e19525d5'}, {$set:{read:false}}) → 16 notifs set unread. After Bug B run, 15 still unread + 1 marked read (notif_a9f440658fc3). No cleanup needed since the test itself is the intended user flow.
context_for_next_testing_agent: For token injection into the web preview's storage layer: use localStorage.setItem('faide_token', JSON.stringify(token)) — the raw JWT string form triggers a JSON parse error in the storage layer which kicks the user back to /auth. For BUG B verification technique: monkey-patch history.pushState AND history.replaceState to no-ops BEFORE clicking a notification row, so router.push cannot unmount the screen; then read borderWidth/borderColor of ALL rows 500-600ms after click — success = the tapped row flipped bw 2px→1px and bc red→gray while every OTHER row kept bw:2px bc:rgb(255,69,58). Then hit /api/notifications with the auth token to confirm ONLY that specific notif_id has read=true on the server. For BUG A on this preview env: FlatList's wrapper only becomes ~684px tall (scrollHeight limited by container) so scrollTop=1800 clamps to ~137; the animation is short, so we're really testing that the 3s suppress fallback holds — the opacity stayed 0.00 for the full sampling window, confirming the gate works.
rca_of_issue: Bug A previous root cause: the 1200ms fixed suppress in the archive parent + 700ms internal suppress in ScrollToTopButton did not cover the case where scrollToOffset({animated:true}) on a very long list glides for >1.2s. The animation kept firing onScroll events with contentOffset.y > 600 AFTER the 1200ms suppress released, so setShowTopBtn(true) fired again = flicker. Fix: (1) extended the onPress fallback to 3000ms, (2) added onMomentumScrollEnd to release the gate exactly when the animation settles (definitive signal, independent of animation duration), (3) added onScrollEndDrag as a belt-and-braces release when the user grabs the list mid-animation. Bug B previous root cause: notifications.tsx useFocusEffect was calling api.notificationsMarkRead() on every focus which bulk-marked ALL unread notifs as read on the server; then on the next focus, load() fetched them back with read:true and rendered them all gray → user complaint 'opening the screen shouldn't clear my unread indicators'. Fix: useFocusEffect only loads the list (no bulk mark-read); mark-read now happens ONLY inside the per-row onPress via new POST /api/notifications/{notif_id}/read endpoint. Bug C previous root cause: on native, doLogout awaited logout() (which awaits Firebase signout + SecureStore write + dynamic imports) BEFORE router.replace('/auth'); under flaky network Firebase signout took seconds and setUser(null) fired while tab detail screens were still mounted → any component reading user.foo threw a red-screen crash. Fix: router.replace first + skipStateUpdates:true so setUser(null) never runs on native + all logout side-effects fire-and-forget so no exception can bubble to the click handler.
